result.title: Ensemble-Aware Structural Encoding (EASE): Conditioning Protein Encoders on Peptide Conformational Ensembles
result.summary: Protein foundation models provide transferable representations for downstream peptide prediction tasks. However, existing representations typically reduce a peptide to a single sequence or structure, which may miss conformational variability relevant to key peptide properties, including antibacterial activity, hemolysis, toxicity, stability, and binding. For example, protease resistance correlates more strongly with conformational dynamics measured by hydrogen exchange than with average helicity. Therefore, we introduce Ensemble-Aware Structural Encoding (EASE), a framework for effectively extracting structural information from conformational ensembles for peptide representation. To extract useful information from noisy conformers, EASE selects central conformers representing a peptide's major structural states and fuses their individual representations with a permutation-invariant operator to produce a peptide-level representation for downstream prediction. We then evaluate our framework on six peptide property-prediction tasks under leakage-controlled splits. Against matched single-structure baselines, EASE improves performance consistently on six tasks with a mean absolute gain of about 3.0% across two structural encoders. Gains keep growing as we add conformers through K=20. A single peptide conformer therefore provides a limited basis for structural representation, whereas our framework distilling and fusing multiple conformers yields a more informative representation.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 EASE 框架：从肽的构象集合中选出代表主要结构状态的中央构象，再用置换不变算子融合各构象表示得到肽级表示，在六个泄漏受控的肽性质预测任务上相对单结构基线平均提升约 3.0%。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「从含噪多构象中筛选代表样本再置换不变聚合」的思路，可能为 LVR 中多假设/多视觉证据的筛选与融合、以及聚合时的信息坍缩问题提供方法线索，但需核查该融合是否保留可区分的细节信息。
